headline: Fog clears to a sunny, low-to-mid 70s Thursday; a weak front brings rain and wind Friday into Saturday, then cooler weather.
summary: As of Thursday morning, dense fog in parts of western Washington, including western Skagit and northwestern Snohomish Counties (Everett and Marysville area) and the Pacific coast, was expected to clear by about 1 PM. Forecasters expect it to be less widespread than in recent days. After that, high pressure brings sunshine and highs in the low to mid 70s, the warmest day of the stretch. A weak front arrives Friday into Saturday with a round of rain and breezy southwest winds around Puget Sound, with stronger winds in the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Rain totals are forecast at about a quarter to half inch in the Cascades and a few hundredths to a tenth of an inch elsewhere. Snow levels (the elevation where rain turns to snow) drop to around 4,500-5,000 ft Friday night into Saturday, with an inch of snow or less, mainly in the North Cascades. Saturday night into Sunday turns drier and cooler, with Sunday morning lows mostly in the upper 30s to low 40s. Some Cascade valleys could fall to around freezing, which matters for gardens, but that risk is only about 30%. Highs midweek are in the low to mid 60s, with another chance of light rain Tuesday. Forecasters are fairly confident in the front and the cooler pattern behind it. After Wednesday, computer models disagree on whether the cool trough lingers or high pressure returns. On the water, a Gale Watch covers the Strait of Juan de Fuca and the coastal waters from late tonight through Friday evening, though gale-force gusts are possible but not certain. A Small Craft Advisory covers the central and eastern Strait from 2 PM Thursday to 3 AM Friday.
changes: The morning update added Dense Fog Advisories for the Everett/Marysville area, the northern Washington coast and Grays Harbor coast, and the waters, expiring by early afternoon. The Friday-Saturday front and the cooler outlook stayed essentially the same.
